options.title: The fourth field
options.telling: Open on the CEO's own sentence — client, product, money — and show, level by level, that nothing in ReconKering follows the meaning. Then hold Gucci's reset against the house's structure to show what a fourth field would have read before the move was made.
options.why: Both documents agree on the gap; this telling lets the briefing's evidence and the paper's structure carry each other, which is the strongest shape for an executive reader who already believes in AI.

options.title: The coherence ledger
options.telling: Read each announced reset — store network, leather-goods priority, see-now-buy-now — against five levels of the house and record which level it reinforces and which it strains. The dossier becomes a ledger the boardroom can reread after the half-year results.
options.why: Most rigorous, and the tables do the talking; costs more because every reset is read at every level and the counterfactual pass asks what the last such move did.

options.title: What the CEO already said
options.telling: Build the entire case from de Meo's dated, on-the-record statements and the group's own filings — nothing inferred, every line anchored — so the reader can check each sentence against its source in the room.
options.why: Cheapest and safest for a careful counterpart in pre-results mode; thinner on the structural argument the working paper makes.
